title: Fix Landing CTAs and restore functional TREY-C Security UI (frontend)

requirements.summary: Ensure Landing page CTAs reliably navigate and are never blocked by overlays/layering issues.
acceptanceCriteria: On the Home (/) page, clicking "Order Now" triggers a route change (no dead click).
On the Home (/) page, clicking "Get Started" triggers a route change (no dead click).
On the Home (/) page, clicking "Learn More" triggers a route change (no dead click).
Buttons are not blocked by any full-screen/absolute-positioned layers (no element overlays capturing pointer events).
No console errors are emitted when clicking the buttons (in a production build).

file_operations.description: Fix click reliability for the "Get Started", "Learn More", and "Order Now" CTAs by auditing stacking contexts and overlay layers in the hero/gradient background and ensuring decorative absolute-positioned layers do not capture pointer events (e.g., ensure background/decoration wrappers are non-interactive while CTA containers remain interactive).

Validate and adjust layout/z-index interactions between the sticky header, main container padding, and the Landing page content so the hero section cannot sit under/behind a pointer-capturing layer; ensure the primary CTA region remains the topmost interactive layer on the Landing page.

requirements.summary: Audit and fix other primary CTAs/navigation interactions (especially BrandHeader and marketing pages) so every visible action is clickable and has a valid handler/state.
acceptanceCriteria: All primary navigation actions in the header (BrandHeader) are clickable and navigate correctly on both desktop and mobile (including the mobile menu buttons).
No button that appears enabled is a no-op (every visible CTA performs its expected action).
If a button must be disabled due to auth/state, the UI clearly indicates disabled state and provides an English explanation (e.g., tooltip, inline text, or toast).

file_operations.description: Audit and harden header interactions: ensure all desktop Links and mobile menu buttons reliably trigger navigation (including Admin and Cart actions), and prevent accidental no-ops by ensuring mobile menu items are real buttons (e.g., correct button type) and not impacted by overlay/pointer-event issues from the Sheet menu.

requirements.summary: Replace the placeholder TREY-C Security admin UI with a functional dashboard backed by real backend calls and resilient error handling.
acceptanceCriteria: The admin "Security Dashboard" section renders real data (not hardcoded stub values) when the backend is available.
Admins can toggle security enabled/disabled from the UI and see the updated state reflected after the mutation completes.
Admins can view security stats (allowed/denied/throttled counts) and a list of recent security events.
If the backend does not support security (e.g., older deployment), the UI shows a clear English error state and does not crash or spin forever.

file_operations.description: Replace stubbed/disabled query with a real react-query hook that reads TREY-C security configuration from the backend actor when available; include robust try/catch handling to surface a clear English error when the backend capability is missing or fails.

Replace stubbed/disabled query with a real react-query hook that reads TREY-C security stats from the backend actor when available; include graceful handling for unsupported backend deployments (show error state rather than infinite loading).

Replace stubbed/disabled query with a real react-query hook that reads recent TREY-C security events from the backend actor when available (supporting a limit parameter); ensure type alignment with backend event shape and add graceful fallback error messaging for unsupported backends.

Replace throwing stub mutations with real mutations that update/toggle TREY-C security configuration and trigger appropriate query invalidations; ensure mutation errors are surfaced as clear English messages suitable for admin UI display (and handle older backend deployments by returning a clear unsupported-feature error).

Replace the AdminUnavailableSection placeholder with a functional "Security Dashboard" UI: read live config/stats/events using the security hooks, provide an enabled/disabled toggle, show stats counters and a recent-events list, and show a clear English unsupported/error state if backend capability is missing (no crashes/spinners).

Ensure the updated TreyCSecuritySection is still correctly lazy-loaded and rendered in the admin panel tabs/sections, and that its loading/error states align with the admin dashboard UX (no hardcoded placeholder messaging).

If needed to support the functional security dashboard UX, adjust/extend security-related query keys (config/stats/events) to ensure cache invalidation/refetching behavior is correct and consistent for admin mutations.

requirements.summary: Implement a working TREY-C security protection modal/banner that informs users without breaking underlying clickability.
acceptanceCriteria: A TREY-C security modal/banner renders with English text indicating protection status.
The modal/banner can be dismissed via an explicit control and does not trap the user on the page.
While visible, the modal does not block critical CTAs unless it is intentionally modal; if it is modal, it must provide an obvious close/dismiss action and restore clickability after dismissal.
After dismissal, the Home page buttons remain clickable and functional.

file_operations.description: Implement the TREY-C security protection UI as a dismissible banner or lightweight modal with English status text driven by the live security config hook; ensure overlay/container pointer-event behavior cannot accidentally block underlying CTAs when presented as a banner (and if modal is used, provide an obvious close/dismiss action).

Wire the TREY-C security protection banner/modal into the global layout so it can render across relevant pages (including Home) without interfering with navigation/button clickability; ensure it renders above content visually but does not create an invisible full-screen overlay capturing clicks.

Verify the Landing page remains fully clickable with the TREY-C security protection banner/modal visible and after dismissal; adjust local layering/pointer-events as needed so the banner does not reintroduce dead-click regions on primary CTAs.
